result.title: Typed Decision Models under Prevalence Shift: Decision Training, Calibration, and Implicit Priors
result.comment: 27 pages, 5 figures. Code, protocol and per-example outputs: https://github.com/AbdulRahmanIqbal/tdm-prevalence-shift
result.summary: Typed decision models (TDMs) return a probability over caller-defined options, and Jev is described by its vendor as calibrated. But in deployment class frequencies change, so calibration measured on a fixed test set need not hold where thresholds are applied. Existing evaluations leave two gaps: the gains of vendor decision training have not been separated from those of the backbone under an identical readout, and TDMs have been tested only at the test set's class distribution. We ask whether decision training improves a model over its own backbone, and whether a TDM's calibration and thresholds withstand prevalence (label) shift as well as a fine-tuned classifier's. We compare three TDMs (Jev, Tev1-4B, Nimble-9B), their base models and two trained classifiers on identical decisions from five public datasets under simulated shift, with 35 paired tests fixed before any test was computed. First, decision training is not uniformly beneficial: Nimble-9B, which differs from Qwen3.5-9B only by a LoRA adapter, is better calibrated on intent tasks but 12.0 Macro-F1 points worse on financial sentiment. Second, under moderate shift Jev's expected calibration error (ECE) and threshold risk grow significantly more than a fine-tuned DeBERTa's only on financial sentiment, by 1.7 and 2.5 percentage points; averaged over 2,000 shift scenarios (exploratory), the gap is at most one point on every dataset. Third, EM prior correction with the model's mean development prediction as its prior needs no labels and lowers Jev's ECE under shift by 2.7 and 1.8 points on the two datasets where it is highest, although labelled recalibration lowers it far more. The three TDMs we tested are neither uniformly better than their backbones nor uniquely fragile under shift; for calibration, their main weakness is the miscalibration they already have without shift. We release all inputs, code and outputs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在模拟标签频率偏移下，用 35 项预注册配对检验比较三种 typed decision models 与其 backbone 及微调分类器的校准（ECE）与阈值风险，以分离 decision training 自身增益，并检验一种无需标签、以开发集平均预测为先验的 EM 校正。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一 readout 下把训练机制增益与 backbone 增益分离」的协议，可能为核查 LVR 推理机制是否真带来增益（贡献分配）提供借鉴；而校准与阈值在分布偏移下是否稳健，可供核查 latent 证据筛选类评价的可靠性。纯文本分类任务，与视觉推理无直接关系，属方法线索。
